title: Headless Anki loses AnkiWeb login -> created cards never sync to devices
description:
The anki-headless container bundles FooSoft AnkiConnect (master) which is incompatible with the pinned Anki 24.11. addNote routes through removed/changed APIs (startEditing -> requireReset, plus many 'deprecated: byName/model/...' warnings). On the headless build this triggers a re-entrant aqt.main.onAppMsg->handleImport->aqt.utils.showInfo MODAL that Xvfb/no-user can't dismiss, which jams the GUI event loop. Symptom: cards get created (addNote limps through) but AnkiConnect 'sync' returns {result:null} yet never uploads to AnkiWeb because the stuck modal blocks it. Confirmed: a fresh 'docker compose restart anki' clears the modal and a single sync (before any new addNote) completes cleanly. So created cards never reach the user's devices without a manual restart+sync.

ROOT CAUSE: AnkiConnect version vs Anki 24.11 mismatch (deploy/anki-headless/Dockerfile fetches FooSoft/anki-connect master).

FIX OPTIONS: (a) bundle an AnkiConnect build that supports Anki 24.x (e.g. the current AnkiWeb release of addon 2055492159, or a maintained fork) — preferred; (b) pin Anki to a version matching the bundled AnkiConnect; (c) suppress/auto-dismiss the modal. Then add auto-sync-on-create (call AnkiConnect 'sync' after addNote) so cards reach AnkiWeb without manual intervention, and a test asserting a created note is uploaded. Discovered during flashgen-19i real-world testing 2026-06-16.
notes: IMPLEMENTED + verified server-side 2026-06-16 (commit 8baf6b3). flashgen-sync addon does programmatic AnkiWeb login (col.sync_login -> pm.set_sync_key) on profile_did_open, ALWAYS refreshing the key from ANKIWEB_USERNAME/ANKIWEB_PASSWORD in .env -> durable by construction. 60s background sync pushes AnkiConnect-created cards. Swapped FooSoft AnkiConnect -> Anki Connect Plus (fixes requireReset/showInfo modal on 24.11). Verified: programmatic login succeeds + persists across 2 restarts (no GUI prompt); addNote no modal; card created via live MCP -> 'sync ok'. AWAITING user device confirmation that the auto-sync test card (Default deck, tag flashgen-autosync-test, '自動同期のテストです') appears on iPhone/Desktop -> then close. Known follow-up: fresh/empty volume needs an initial FULL_DOWNLOAD which the addon currently skips (safe-full-download heuristic) — not needed while volume is intact.
close_reason: Fixed + confirmed end-to-end on a user device. flashgen-sync addon does durable programmatic AnkiWeb login (col.sync_login -> pm.set_sync_key, refreshed every startup from ANKIWEB_* in .env) + 60s background auto-sync; swapped FooSoft AnkiConnect -> Anki Connect Plus (no more requireReset/showInfo modal on 24.11). User confirmed a card created via the live MCP auto-synced to AnkiWeb and appeared on their device with no manual action. Commit 8baf6b3.

title: search_notes wildcard bridge fails for queries ≥6 chars (Anki per-term wildcard cap)
description: Reported by the Japanese-language agent using FlashGen MCP. The bare-word narrowing query builds ONE wildcard-interleaved term (Japanese:*c1*c2*...*cn*). Anki silently returns 0 matches when a single term exceeds ~6 '*' wildcards, so bare-word queries of >=6 chars (e.g. full-sentence dedup checks) return 0 hits with no error — reads as 'no duplicate exists'. Empirically bisected: 5 chars (6 stars) works, 6 chars (7 stars) fails, char-independent. Verified fix direction: chunk the interleave into <=5-char groups emitted as separate ANDed Japanese:*...* terms; cross-group ordering loss is corrected by the existing Python post-filter (strip furigana, contiguous substring). Applies to match_field japanese_tts/japanese and the 'any' OR-branch.
notes: ROOT CAUSE CORRECTION: not an Anki wildcard cap (13-star single term verified fine directly against AnkiConnect). Real bug: furigana convention puts spaces before UNANNOTATED units (その 報[ほう] 告[こく]は ある…); strip_furigana_markup keeps those spaces, so the post-filter substring check failed on any fragment spanning such a boundary — silent 0 hits on full-sentence dedup. The reporting agent's 'confirmed' chunked query contained quotes/colons → raw-syntax path → skipped the buggy post-filter, which produced the false confirmation. Fix ed076cb: despace (U+0020/U+00A0/U+3000) both sides in the japanese_tts and any post-filters; narrowing stays one interleaved term. Verified live: その報告はあ and full sentence now 1 hit.
close_reason: Fixed in ed076cb (space-insensitive post-filter), deployed, verified live on the exact reported repro.

title: AnkiWeb credentials stored/exposed in plaintext in flashgen-anki container env
description:
While verifying flashgen-3c6, 'docker inspect flashgen-mcp' (and the anki container env) exposed ANKIWEB_USERNAME and ANKIWEB_PASSWORD in PLAINTEXT as container environment variables. Anyone with host/docker access (or anyone who runs docker inspect) can read the AnkiWeb password. The value was also surfaced into an agent transcript during this session.

RISK: AnkiWeb account credential disclosure -> full access to the user's Anki collection / sync, and the password may be reused elsewhere.

REMEDIATION:
1. ROTATE the AnkiWeb password now (it was printed to a transcript this session).
2. Stop passing the password as a plain compose 'environment:' var. Options: Docker secrets (compose 'secrets:' + read from /run/secrets), or keep it only in the gitignored deploy/.env referenced via env_file (still readable via docker inspect, so secrets are better), or inject at runtime from a secret store.
3. Confirm deploy/.env is gitignored and was never committed (git log -p check).
4. Audit anything else in the compose env (the MCP bearer token, OPENAI/GEMINI keys) for the same exposure.

ACCEPTANCE: AnkiWeb password rotated; credentials no longer visible via 'docker inspect' as plaintext env (moved to docker secrets or equivalent); .env confirmed never committed; related secrets audited.
notes: COMPLETE + verified on host. AnkiWeb password rotated by user (new 1Password value set on AnkiWeb, written into deploy/secrets/ankiweb_password via read -rs, never entered any transcript). Host migration: deploy/secrets/{ankiweb_username,ankiweb_password} created (600); ANKIWEB_* stripped from host .env (backup removed); rsynced new compose+addon; built anki; up -d recreated both containers. VERIFIED: docker inspect flashgen-mcp has NO ANKIWEB_PASSWORD; flashgen-anki env only ANKIWEB_*_FILE -> /run/secrets; sync log 'logged into AnkiWeb as ssaito@...; sync key refreshed; sync ok'; mcp /health {ok:true}. .env never committed (git log empty) + gitignored. Filed flashgen-oxu for remaining MCP/OpenAI/Gemini env secrets.
close_reason: Closed

title: Confirm root cause: MCP create_flashcard stores notes verbatim, newlines don't render
description:
The MCP create_flashcard path appears to store the 'notes' field verbatim without converting \n into HTML line breaks. Anki fields are HTML. In HTML, a literal '\n' renders as the text '\n', and a real newline character collapses to whitespace unless the card template CSS uses white-space: pre-wrap. The only thing that reliably produces a visible line break is the
tag. OBSERVATION: Pre-MCP cards created via the local script have
tags for line breaks (verified in Anki via Cmd+Shift+X HTML editor) and render correctly. MCP-created cards do not, so newlines in notes display wrong. HYPOTHESIS: The local flashgen.py script converts \n ->
before writing the field; the MCP path skips this. The japanese/furigana fields render correctly (the [reading] furigana markup survives), suggesting they go through a different, non-escaping code path than notes. GOAL OF THIS BUG: confirm the exact root cause before fixing. Specifically determine: 1. Where the local script converts \n ->
(which function/module) and whether notes is HTML-escaped there. 2. Where the MCP create_flashcard handler writes the notes field and what (if any) transform it applies. 3. Whether notes is HTML-escaped at all in either path, and whether the literal stored value is '\n' (two chars) or a real newline char. 4. Confirm japanese/furigana fields take a separate code path that does not escape. ACCEPTANCE: A written explanation in this issue's notes identifying the precise divergence between the two paths, with file:line references.
acceptance_criteria: Notes field on this issue documents: (1) local-script \n->br conversion location, (2) MCP notes write location + transform, (3) whether/where HTML-escaping happens, (4) confirmation furigana takes separate path. Includes file:line refs.
notes:
DEFINITIVE ROOT CAUSE (resolved from ground-truth: user pasted a real MCP-created card's Notes field). The stored Notes field contains '<br>' (HTML-escaped
), e.g.: '夢中[むちゅう]になる<br> 助詞[じょし]は...' That renders on the card as the VISIBLE TEXT '
'. It is NEITHER a literal backslash-n NOR a collapsed real newline — it is an escaped
tag. MECHANISM (reproduced exactly, see python check): - The MCP client (Claude) sends the notes field with line breaks already as literal '
' HTML tags (NOT \n). - notes_to_html (src/flashgen.py:125-131) runs html.escape(notes) BEFORE injecting breaks, so '
' -> '<br>'. The subsequent .replace(chr(10),'
') finds no real newlines, so nothing is restored. - html.escape('夢中になる
助詞') == '夢中になる<br> 助詞' => matches the user's field byte-for-byte. This ELIMINATES the two earlier candidate conditions: - NOT stale container (condition B): the escaping proves notes_to_html IS running on the deployed server. A pre-b42829b container would store raw
and render correctly. So flashgen-mcp:latest is current enough to have notes_to_html. - NOT literal-backslash-n (condition A): the field has
/<br>, not backslash-n. WHY LOCAL WORKS, MCP DOESN'T: the divergence is the line-break representation the caller supplies, not the code path (both call notes_to_html). Local CLI input carries REAL newlines (LLM output via json_repair), which notes_to_html escapes-then-converts correctly. The MCP client supplies literal
tags, which get escaped into visible text. FIX (validated in python, see flashgen-3c6): normalize ALL break representations to a real newline BEFORE html.escape, then convert real newline ->
. Specifically: regex <\s*br\s*/?\s*> (case-insensitive) -> \n; literal \r\n/\n/\r -> \n; real \r\n/\r -> \n; html.escape(quote=False); replace \n ->
. Verified:
input, real newline, literal backslash-n all yield correct
; genuine HTML-special chars in definitions (< & >) still escape safely. NO FURTHER VERIFICATION NEEDED for root cause. Deploy-freshness check is moot (proven not stale).
close_reason:
Root cause definitively confirmed from ground-truth card data: MCP client sends notes line breaks as literal
tags; notes_to_html escapes them to <br> (visible text). Not stale container, not literal-\n. Fix validated, handed to flashgen-3c6.

title: Add SSH-over-Cloudflare-tunnel break-glass + disable Tailscale key expiry
description: flashgen-qqq follow-up: Lightsail browser SSH is incompatible with Tailscale-only sshd binding (sshd not on public iface), so it cannot be break-glass. Add two resiliency measures: (1) disable Tailscale key expiry for the flashgen-mcp node so the sole path doesn't auto-expire; (2) add a second independent access path via SSH over the existing cloudflared tunnel: ingress ssh.ssaito.net -> ssh://127.0.0.1:22, DNS route, gated by Cloudflare Access. Neither exposes a public port.
notes: RESUMED 2026-06-08: Cloudflare Zero Trust now activated (was a billing issue on Cloudflare's side, since fixed — not connectivity). Tailscale key expiry disabled; ssh.ssaito.net tunnel ingress live; Cloudflare Access self-hosted app (team round-poetry-23ec.cloudflareaccess.com) gates it with policy auth_email (Allow Emails=ssaito@alum.mit.edu, One-time PIN). title: Rotate FLASHGEN_MCP bearer token (exposed in prior docker inspect)
description:
The MCP bearer token appeared in plaintext in 'docker inspect flashgen-mcp' during the flashgen-w07/oxu sessions before the file-secrets migration. The disclosure vector is now closed (token lives in deploy/secrets/flashgen_mcp_token, mounted at /run/secrets, no longer in env/inspect), but the VALUE itself was exposed and should be rotated.

HOW THE TOKEN WORKS:
- app.py reads FLASHGEN_MCP_TOKEN via flashgen.read_secret() at IMPORT time (app.py:17) into _MCP_TOKEN.
- _check_bearer() requires 'Authorization: Bearer <_MCP_TOKEN>' on /mcp (app.py:24-28).
- The OAuth token endpoint just ECHOES _MCP_TOKEN as the access_token (app.py:257); clients use token_endpoint_auth_method=none. So Claude obtains the token automatically via the OAuth flow — there is no manual token to paste into Claude's config.
- Because the token is read at import, the container must be RESTARTED/RECREATED to pick up a new secret-file value.

ROTATION STEPS:
1. Generate a new token locally (do NOT echo it to any transcript), e.g.:
     python3 -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))'
   (current token is 43 chars = token_urlsafe(32); keep similar strength.)
2. Write it to the host secret file WITHOUT printing the value, e.g. paste via a read prompt:
     ssh flashgen-mcp 'read -rs T && printf %s "$T" > /home/ubuntu/flashgen/deploy/secrets/flashgen_mcp_token && chmod 600 /home/ubuntu/flashgen/deploy/secrets/flashgen_mcp_token'
   (Then type/paste the new value at the silent prompt.)
3. Recreate the mcp container so _MCP_TOKEN reloads:
     ssh flashgen-mcp 'cd /home/ubuntu/flashgen/deploy && docker compose up -d --force-recreate flashgen-mcp'
4. Reconnect FlashGen in Claude (claude.ai connectors / MCP): disconnect+reconnect or re-authenticate so it re-runs OAuth and receives the new token. Existing sessions holding the OLD token will start getting 401 until re-auth.
5. VERIFY (no value printed):
     # old token -> 401, new token -> 200
     ssh flashgen-mcp 'T=$(cat /home/ubuntu/flashgen/deploy/secrets/flashgen_mcp_token); curl -s -o /dev/null -w "newtok:%{http_code}\n" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" -d "{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":1,\"method\":\"tools/list\"}"'
     curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'health:%{http_code}\n' https://mcp.ssaito.net/health
     # In Claude, confirm a FlashGen tool (e.g. validate_flashcard) still works end-to-end.

ACCEPTANCE: new token in deploy/secrets/flashgen_mcp_token; container recreated; old token rejected (401); Claude reconnected and a FlashGen MCP tool call succeeds; old value no longer valid anywhere.
notes: ROTATED 2026-07-09: New token generated on remote host directly into deploy/secrets/flashgen_mcp_token (43 chars, never printed to any transcript). Container force-recreated and healthy. Verified: new token -> 200, old token -> 401, https://mcp.ssaito.net/health -> 200. Old-token backup deleted from host. title: Validator: keep furigana annotations whole instead of even-splitting per kanji
description: normalize_furigana_annotation (flashgen.py) re-derives per-kanji furigana by evenly slicing the reading whenever a multi-kanji run's reading length divides by the kanji count. This is reading-unsafe by construction, e.g. 試着室[しちゃくしつ] -> 試[しち] 着[ゃく] 室[しつ] (着[ゃく] even starts with a standalone small ゃ). Whole-unit annotation is always reading-safe (the bracket sits over the whole run, no boundary to misplace) and respects the LLM's own furigana grouping, which is the right division of labor since the LLM owns furigana insertion. Change: make normalize_furigana_annotation always return the whole ' {kanji}[{reading}]' unit, dropping the even-split branch. The existing regex prefix [U+0020 U+3000]* + one-ASCII-space replacement already handles ALL spacing normalization (collapse multiple, full-width->ASCII, insert-when-missing, between adjacent runs, after kana prefix), so no new space-fixing pass is needed. split_evenly becomes dead code (remove); check whether is_kanji_text is still used.
design: Reduce normalize_furigana_annotation to 'return f" {kanji}[{reading}]"'. Keep ANNOTATED_KANJI_RE leading-space prefix and reading capture [^]]+ (permissive, not kana-only). Keep intentional leading space at start-of-field (Anki furigana convention).
acceptance_criteria: normalize_furigana_annotation always emits whole 'kanji[reading]' units (no per-kanji even-split); spacing normalization unchanged (one ASCII space before each annotated kanji run); split_evenly removed; test_furigana_normalization.py updated to assert whole-unit outputs and still passes; full suite green.
close_reason: normalize_furigana_annotation now always emits whole 'kanji[reading]' units; dropped the reading-unsafe per-kanji even-split (試着室[しちゃくしつ] -> 試着室[しちゃくしつ], not 試[しち] 着[ゃく] 室[しつ]).
